column6: First priority digit is a clear 5: flat 6-px top bar, open lower-left, tail, like the 5s in 595 and 7475. The duplicate 572 is resolved on A035-L22 (672). Specks left of 572 and the tick after 7475 are not characters.

First priority digit is a 6, not a 5: short sloped top like the 6s in 670 (L15) and in 79465 on this line, not the flat 7-px bar of the 5s in 559 and 573. The lower bowl closes at the left after a 2-row break. Tiebreaker used: 572 is also on A012-L16, where the 5 is clear, and 672 is unused elsewhere. Tick after MANCH is a stray mark.

The 0 is clean: one open counter and no waist, like the 0s in 5032 and 1077, so it is not an 8 (18). The dot to the left is a speck. Printed as read; the duplicate priority 10 (also on A027-L20) is in the source.
The 3rd letter after the slash is clearly a K: a stem with upper and lower diagonals. Printed as read; BYLOVO on C207-L09 is a different entry with different coordinates.

Second digit is a 0: at native resolution it has one counter and no waist, while the 8s in 58975, 608 and 638 all have a waist. The bottom is heavy and there is a speck above. 18 is not supported by the print. Printed as read; the duplicate 10 is in the source.

Last longitude digit stays ?: heavy ink, a tiny closed counter at the top (like a 9), and a full-width bottom bar (like a 3; the 9s on this page have narrow tails). It cannot be decided between 3 and 9 and may be an overstrike. The dotted vertical mark below it is not a character.

The BE digit after the 8 is a 0 with its left side missing: top arc, right side and bottom are present, with no trace of a 3's middle cusp. The next 0 has lost its right side. The OMSK run 0163-8001 / 8?02 / 8003 settled it. The last longitude digit is an 8 (it has a crossbar).

4th latitude digit stays ?: solid ink in the upper half, then a right stem and a full-width bottom with a small left hook. That is closest to a 3, since the 9s here have narrow tails, the 5s keep a right notch and the 8s a lower-left side. But no 3 on the page has a filled top (possible overstrike), so it stays undecided between 3 and 9. It is not a 4.

Last longitude digit stays ?: the top is a solid blob. The right side, the left hook and the bottom bar match this page's 3s; no lower-left side rules out an 8, and the narrow-tailed 9s here do not match. Probably a 3, but the filled top leaves it undecided (3 or 9). The 2 before 10 has lost its base bar but is a 2.
The line is clear as read. Printed as read: the misplaced entry is SZYMANY (L11, ref 8100), typed above SZOLNOK 8075 and SZOMBATHELY 8085 in the source.

The 2nd latitude digit is a 2 with no base bar, like the 2 in 02340 on this line: arc top and a stroke ending at the lower-left corner. The 7s on this page have flat tops and centre stems (native match: 2 0.84, 7 0.57). The 4th digit is a 0 (no crossbar). The BE chart's 3rd digit has a 6's short sloped top and closed lower-left; the glyph is ambiguous. The document settled it: chart 0168 covers 52-56N, the 0168-86xx run is alphabetical (BOBRUYSK 8606 < BREST < CHERNYAKHOVSK 8612), and BREST city (C029-L09) is 5206-02342.
The digit after the hyphen is a clean 0 (one counter, no waist; the 8 in 0380 has a waist). Printed as read; the non-8xxx BE number is in the source.

The digit after the hyphen is a 3. Its left side is open in both halves; the top-left hook and the cusp running left match other 3s on the page. The 8s here have both loops closed. Printed as read; the non-8xxx BE number is in the source.
The first letter is clearly a G. Printed as read; WUSTROW (C293-L27, 5405-01135) is a different place. The dot inside 2493 is a speck.
The first letter is clearly a W. Printed as read; GUSTROW (C091-L37) has different coordinates.
The 4th letter is clearly a P. Printed as read; SLANY (C212-L13, 5014-01405) is a separate entry. The tiny dot below the baseline after 01425 is a speck, not a period.
The 4th letter is clearly an N. Printed as read; SLAPY (C017-L40) has different coordinates.
The B is clear: two bowls on a stem. Letter spacing shows no space after the K. Printed as read; AKTYURINSK is a reading of A002-L07.
TAO AN: the gap between O and A is exactly one character cell, so no N is missing. The 1-px dot in the gap is a speck. Printed as read; it differs from TAO NAN (A037-L07) in the source.
TAO NAN, is clear. Printed as read. The small dot after 82562 (9 px of ink, below the baseline) is a speck; this page's periods and commas are about 35-40 px.
The 3rd letter is clearly an L (no upper diagonal). Printed as read; BYKOVO (A023-L27) is a different entry with different coordinates.

The 3rd latitude digit is a 2 with no base bar: arc top and a diagonal to the lower-left corner. The 7s on this page have flat tops and vertical centre stems (native match: 2 0.74, 7 0.50). The minutes>=60 flag settled it; 6424 also fits the other chart-0075 airfields at 64-66N. The 1-px dot after the 4th longitude digit is a speck.
Six clear, evenly spaced digits follow the hyphen (0 3 6 1 2 0). Only specks lie left of 3932, so no priority is printed. Printed as read; the nonstandard format is in the source.
